contexts.text: Cannot be... apprehended by any human idea.
Man can apprehend no otherwise...
The principles that have been adopted, even the falsest, rule the man...
They then began to believe nothing that they did not apprehend by the senses... Treated of. AC 210. AC 235.
That the case is thus can never be apprehended by the senses, by science, and by philosophy...
The Church... so loved itself, or proprium, that it could no longer apprehend anything of truth... Treated of.
He who attends closely to the sense of the words of one who is speaking, does indeed hear the words, but as it were does not hear; he apprehends only the sense.
The spiritual Angels... instruct (the Soul) about those things which are in the other life, but [only] so far as he is able to apprehend.
Unless there is apprehended by man an idea... he cannot think...
He who confirms false principles, first adopts a principle...
In place of the revelations of the Most Ancient Church, there succeeded doctrinal things, which they first apprehended by the outward senses...
It is exceedingly difficult to say to the apprehension...
He who adopts the principle, that...
They who can apprehend nothing except from such things as there are with man...
He who is not willing to believe before he apprehends these things, can never believe. References.
They are called drunkards who believe nothing except what they apprehend... AC 5120:8.
They who are in the faith of charity... say that there are very few things that they can apprehend, and therefore to think that a thing is not true because they do not apprehend it, is insane.
They who believe nothing, except what they apprehend through sensual and scientific things, are called heroes to drink.
Here Egypt stands for those who believe nothing unless they apprehend it from scientifics...
The principles that a man adopts from early childhood, the Lord never breaks, but bends...
But Spirits to whom bodily and earthly ideas adhere, do not apprehend this...
They do not apprehend that such perception is possible...
They who from simplicity of heart believe the Word as they apprehend it in the letter...
When the Most Ancient Church... saw (the things that are in the world), or apprehended them by some sense, they did not think about them... AC 2896. AC 2896.
There was perceived... the sphere of those who believe nothing except what they apprehend by the senses.

It was said to them that they ought not to doubt because they do not apprehend; for if nothing is believed except what is apprehended, nothing is believed about those things which are of interior nature, still less those which are of eternal life. Hence is the insanity of our age.
Divine mysteries, which human minds, however they were unfolded, would not apprehend, and which many would not be willing to apprehend.

The... beauty of (the inward sense) cannot appear... as if they were apprehended in one idea... This is as when one who hears another speaking attends to the words; he then does not so well apprehend the idea of him who is speaking...
Everyone is able to apprehend merely from the fact...
The Jews, who were unwilling to apprehend anything whatever, except what was according to the senses...
The Rational first conceived does not apprehend this...
Then are dispelled the shades of fallacies, and it is then a matter of no account with him that he does not apprehend.
This is the case with all Truths Divine; if the (first) Rational be consulted about them they can never be believed, for they are entirely above its apprehension. Example(s). AC 2657:5.

Unless the interior sight with man continually inflows into his outward sight... never can the latter apprehend or discern any object; for it is the interior sight which, through the eye, apprehends those things which the eye sees.
The rest... shall be explained as far as [is possible to] the apprehension.
These can never receive any faith, unless they first apprehend in some way how it can be so.
At this day with the men of the Christian Church, intellectual good begins to perish... The cause is that they believe nothing but what they apprehend by the senses.

The feet and the hoofs with which the streams and the waters are disturbed () = scientifics from sensual and natural things, from which they reason concerning the arcana of faith; nor believe before they are apprehended by means of them; which is never to believe...
When the man of the Church thus apprehended these (representatives)...
Human rational truth does not apprehend Divine things, because they are above the sphere of its understanding... AC 2209.
Man, from appearances, cannot apprehend that... AC 2196:13.
Yea, in natural things themselves the Rational is blind, as for instance, it is unable to apprehend how (the antipodes) can stand upon their feet...
When a man adopts any principle...
Heavenly arcana have this characteristic, that although they are above all apprehension, still everyone forms for himself some idea about them...
This they do according to their apprehension...
Such do they become who hatch doctrinal things from reasoning, and believe nothing unless they first apprehend...
Any principle... once adopted, can be confirmed...
Doctrine is said to regard rational things, when no other truth of doctrine is acknowledged, than what can be apprehended by reason...
If truths were set forth nakedly from a Divine origin, they would never be received, but would transcend all man's apprehension, thus also belief... Example(s).
Since the human Rational is such, [everything] is spoken in the Word according to man's apprehension... AC 2533:2.
Under Angel, see this reference.
Man cannot apprehend anything doctrinal that is purely spiritual and celestial, that is, Divine, because it infinitely transcends his apprehension, thus also his belief...
This (insane) principle is to deny all things, or to say in his heart that he cannot believe them until he is convinced by those things which he can apprehend or feel...
No one can apprehend higher things from lower ones...

They who have blinded themselves through this, that they were unwilling to believe anything that they did not apprehend by the senses, so that at last they believed nothing at all, were formerly called serpents of the tree of knowledge; for from the sensual things and the fallacies thence, which easily fall into the apprehension and belief of man, they reasoned much, and led many astray.
This does not fall into the apprehension even when most highly enlightened through those things which are of the light of the world.
He is unwilling to believe (the arcana of faith) except through those things that are in the world; yea, that he should apprehend them by means of sensual things...
From this he gets a sphere of perception...
That they saw the Lord... did not make anyone blessed, but that they apprehended with the understanding...
By Beersheba is signified human rational things again adjoined to the doctrine of faith... and thus doctrine made for human apprehension.
This does not appear to the sense, or the apprehension...
No otherwise can man apprehend, than that he who permits also wills.
Under Appearance, see this reference, and at AC 3362. AC 3387:2.
Evil Spirits cannot at all apprehend that they do not live from themselves...

The daughter of Egypt stands for the affection of reasoning from scientifics about the truths of faith, whether they are so; thus for the religiosity that rises forth thence, which is such, that nothing is believed unless it is apprehended by the senses. References.
Since the inward sense describes these things... it cannot be otherwise than that they should be expounded, however much they may appear to be above the apprehension.
It is good that apprehends...
There are innumerable things which the natural man does not apprehend... and what he does apprehend, he believes either not to exist, or not to be so.

[When] a man no longer believes anything but what he can apprehend sensually and scientifically, he then perverts and extinguishes the things that are of the doctrine of faith, and most of all those which are of charity. Signified.
The ideas (of the Angels of the interior Heaven) not only exceed apprehension, but even belief.
The Rational is such that it can never apprehend Divine things; for it is finite, and this cannot apprehend those things which are of the infinite...

Since the spiritual have not a perception whether it is so, there is given to them what appears to be truth, and this according to their Rational, that is, according to their apprehension, for so it is received. Everyone is permitted to believe truths as he apprehends them; otherwise there would be no reception...
By rational truth is meant that which appears to be true according to the apprehension, or before the Rational.
Truths Divine themselves... exceed all their rational apprehension, thus all their belief...
The Lord replied according to their apprehension...

The first of the confirmation of truth is that it is called Divine; immediately they have an idea of what is holy, which gives a universal confirmation to each and all things that are said, and this although they do not apprehend it; but still the things that are said must be adapted to their apprehension; for it is not enough that man knows that it is so...
No matter of faith, not even the deepest arcanum, is ever apprehended by any man without some rational, and even natural, idea...
The Philistines envied him = that those who were in the mere science of knowledges did not apprehend.
That the Lord disposed truths so that they were adapted to the apprehension and genius of those who are not in life, but in the doctrinals of faith. Signified.
A man is able to apprehend this from the understanding, although the will dissents, or even goes into the contrary.
Although most clearly expounded, yet when the knowledge is wanting, they are not apprehended.
(These things) are adapted to the understanding and apprehension of the Angels...
They who are in the affection of self and of the world can by no means apprehend these things...

Thus the Word could be written, that it should be according to the apprehension of the man who read it, and according to the understanding of the Angels with the man... If it had been otherwise, it would not have been adapted to the understanding of readers, especially of that time...
Yet are such things adapted to the understanding and apprehension of Angels, also to the apprehension of Spirits.
For the sake of man's apprehension, the Lord's Divine is distinguished into Divine Good and Divine Truth.
Reasonings about goods and truths, that they are not, except in so far as they are assumed... (Signified by the eagles at the carcase.)
Divine or Infinite things are only apprehended from finite ones...
The things now adduced are indeed such as to fall into the apprehension of but very few...
Man is led... by many affections of good and truth that are not genuine... but are only useful for the apprehending of them...
This arcanum... cannot be manifest except to an apprehension instructed...
They who are not regenerate can apprehend nothing whatever about this thing.
The heavenly form... is far above the ideas of the forms that man can ever apprehend from worldly things, even by means of analytics.
They live at last in such... stupidity, that hardly anything of what is human, as to apprehension, is left in them.

The rest care nothing for such (spiritual knowledges)... and such a one would say that he apprehends nothing about them... But if such things are said to him as relate to his business in the world, although they are very recondite... this he not only apprehends, but also perceives the interior things.
This is how it is with man's apprehension...
These (truths) cannot come to man's intuition and apprehension until good becomes the primary agent...
What a man loves, he easily draws in and apprehends, but with difficulty that which he does not love.
They who are in mere outward things cannot apprehend what inward things are, thus cannot be affected by them; for no one is affected by those things which he does not apprehend. Example(s).
What a man does not see from the Natural he does not apprehend.
They who are sensual... rarely apprehend anything about the things that are of Heaven...
This is Infinite, and thus transcends all apprehension, even the angelic.
Unless spiritual things are presented representatively in what is natural, thus by means of such things as are in the world, they are not at all apprehended.
All truths of faith that man draws in from early childhood, are apprehended by means of such objects, and thence ideas, as are from the light of the world...
There was an interpreter between them = that then spiritual things are apprehended altogether otherwise. Explained.
The more interior such things are, the more remote they are from the apprehension of men to whom the things of the world and the body are alone pleasant and delightful.
If there are any things that they do not apprehend, they reject them to the sides, and say, that they do not as yet understand them, and still remain in the faith of truth.
Those are said to be in simple good who... believe the Word simply as to its literal sense, each according to his apprehension...
The things in the sense of the letter are such as accommodate themselves to the apprehension of the simple...
Naked spiritual things man does not apprehend...
Man is such that what he sees and apprehends from his Sensual, he believes; and what he does not see, nor apprehend from his Sensual, he does not believe...
He made signs to the eyes of the people = confirmation to the apprehension.
If the natural man concludes with himself, that nothing is to be believed except what he apprehends, he then casts himself into enormous errors. Explained.
These things no one can know from himself, for man does not apprehend [anything] except what has been in the way of the senses...
The sense of the letter is according to the apprehension of simple men, in order that they may be introduced into interior truths themselves.
That the people may hear when I speak with thee = that those who are of the Spiritual Church may apprehend Divine things... To hear = to perceive, thus to apprehend.
Truth Divine is not received by anyone, unless it is accommodated to the apprehension... for human minds do not at first apprehend [anything] except earthly and worldly things. AC 8920:2. AC 8922.
The second religiosity is that in which the lumen of nature is everything; those who are in it acknowledge nothing as truth that they do not apprehend...
He who is wise only from the world believes nothing except what the senses apprehend; and what he believes, he believes from the fallacies of the senses...
These truths can indeed be described, but not to the apprehension, except of those who are in the light of Heaven from the Lord...
To be taken () = to be carried away by (the evils of the love of self and of the world).
When such a man comes into Heaven, he apprehends the Word not at all otherwise than according to its inward sense...
(The eyes of the body) are formed to take in earthly and bodily things... they are therefore so gross that they cannot even take in by sight the interior things of nature.
Hence man perceives what is good, and feels it, thus apprehends the quality of it.

These arcana can hardly be apprehended by anyone at this day... It would be quite otherwise if the mind were delighted with heavenly things more than earthly ones, for those things with which a man is delighted are apprehended...

(Such) can no otherwise apprehend the Spiritual than as a purer Natural... Hence it is that by such learned men there is not apprehended the difference between the inward... and the outward... man... Hence also neither can they apprehend anything about faith and love, Heaven and Hell, and the life of man after death. NJHD 47:2, References.
The Angels... apprehend what comes up according to its essence; that is, spiritually.
They who love their evils... can indeed apprehend and after a fashion understand truths from the Word...
The happiness that follows the removal (of the loves of self and the world) is so great as to exceed all man's apprehension.
Rational things are, by many, not apprehended.
(Captus and Comprehendere used synonymously.)

There are very many such in the world, who reject spiritual things because they do not apprehend with the senses... Such were with me... They kept me awake the whole night, and so punished me because I have spoken and written so much about spiritual things, when yet these things cannot be apprehended by such things as are of the sense of the body...

I could come into no spiritual thought... Their Spiritual was represented by them as a leafy cloud... This [was] from their conception that a cloud can feel and perceive nothing, so that it is a mere Natural as with beasts. (Their punishment.)

It was given to say to them... that man never knows anything, as for instance, how the muscles effect actions... there are indefinite things that we do not know... and yet they suppose that unless they know and so apprehend, or as they say, understand with the sense how the case is with spiritual things...

They have now also confessed that they can never perceive anything of what I write about spiritual things; but that they can only apprehend effects when they apprehend the effects with the sense of the body; other things are nothing.
Everything that man apprehends from himself alone is false...
By them that are bound and him that is captured in the eyes () are signified those to whom it is denied to see truths.
